title: Why Scott Chose Dog‑Sleds
topic: Why the British explorer Robert Falcon Scott equipped his Antarctic expedition with motor‑sled dogs (Antarctica, 1910–1912) to conserve sledging manpower

lines: Scott chained a pack of huskies to a sled, wind howling.
The storm ripped his coat, snow stinging his face.
Every step felt like walking on knives.
His crew scoffed, insisting men should pull every load.
They whispered that dogs were useless in such cold.
Scott heard their doubts echo across the ice.
He ordered the dogs forward, refusing to waste any human step.
The huskies surged forward, paws cracking the crust.
Men watched, breath fogging, as distance shrank.
You see, it’s like riding a bike to carry groceries.
Just as a bike spares your legs, the dogs spare your muscles.
Scott knew dogs could haul supplies, letting men conserve strength for glacier.
Without dogs, men would trek for miles, exhausting quickly.
The plan saved weeks of brutal hauling.
Ironically, those dogs were abandoned, never to return to any home.
Their bodies later lay frozen, a silent reminder of sacrifice.
History remembers the pole, not the forgotten pups.

claims.claim: Scott knew dogs could haul supplies, letting men conserve strength for glacier.
